messages:
maya: Noticing a new p99 host cpu tail post-rollout of kernel-prefers-fused (landed 03/20). Impact mainly on short-seq workloads. Repro on staging.

jon: Any flamegraphs? Short workloads should've reduced GPU time not increased host CPU.

maya: Paste from a quick perf-top (3s sampler):
```
parse::tokenize        42%
grpc::writev           15%
kv_store::hot_shard    12%
net::assemble_frame     7%
syscalls/other          24%
```
Looks like more concurrent tokenization + lots of tiny writev syscalls.

felix: Data point: under fused kernel we push more concurrent decodes (GPU finishes faster) -> host preproc becomes the limiter. If minibatch size stayed at 1, tokenization doesn't amortize. Did batching policy change?

maya: No batching code was changed in that PR. Kernel-selector now picks fused for median_seq<32. That increased parallelism.

toni: gRPC traces show many 100-300B payload writes per request. The socket write path calls writev multiple times because our framer treats each token as a separate frame for short outputs. We can coalesce at framer level to emit fewer syscalls.

jon: Also kv hit-rate telemetry dipped during the spike: 97% -> 88% for small sequences. Hypothesis: more simultaneous KV lookups causing lock contention and more cold misses due to eviction under load.

maya: Quick experiment: on one staging box I throttled concurrent decoders to 8 and p99 host CPU dropped ~12%. kv_hit resumed. So throttling helps but we need automatic heuristics.

felix: Suggest two-prong approach: 1) ingress framer coalescing for writes <512B, 2) adaptive minibatching for short seqs up to N (configurable) to amortize tokenization. Both should be low-risk and reversible.

toni: I can prototype coalescing today. Option: maintain a per-connection small-write buffer and flush when >=512B or after 2ms. Should reduce writev count dramatically. Drawback: adds tiny buffering delay but for short outputs 2ms is acceptable.

jon: For KV contention we can add a soft backoff token: if kv_lock_waits/sec > threshold, increase min_batch_size or temporarily accept fewer inflight decoders. Might be simpler than sharding changes.

maya: Agree. Plan: toni deploys framer coalesce to canary; felix adds minibatch tweak and kv-backpressure metric->knob. Rollback if end-to-end latency or tail errors increase.

infra-bot: Deploy scheduled: canary/ingress-framer-coalesce -> eng-runtime-canary-2 by toni at 06:10 UTC

maya: After canary runs we'll compare p99 host CPU, avg grpc writev calls/second, and kv_hit%. If coalesce + minibatch gets us within 5% baseline we're good. If not, we add kernel-selector guard (prefer non-fused for high qps short sequences).

jon: Also capture tcp_nodelay states across hosts. We may want to enable Nagle for internal links or ensure coalesce at app since kernel-level Nagle has tradeoffs.

toni: I'll post canary logs & perf before EOD. Thanks. :wave:
